releases.notes: Reviewed PSP v4 agent protocol and exact release packaging. The first release under the product scheme: the tag is release/4.0.0 and the version is 4.0.0, the archive is named passwall-node_4.0.0_linux_<arch>.tar.gz, and the exact image tag is 4.0.0. The download chain was verified against the published release rather than constructed: the slash-bearing URL serves the asset, the checksum manifest names it exactly once, and sha256sum --check passes. State schema 9 and upgrade contract 1 are unchanged. Published as a pre-release, so no stable pointer moved. Remote upgrades require Linux/systemd, the upgrade helper, and unchanged state schema 9. Docker uses container-managed updates. Docker and Windows end-to-end installation has not been verified, and no end-to-end upgrade on a real host has been performed for this release.

note: THE REVIEWED NODE RELEASE REGISTRY. Every release here was reviewed before it could be offered for remote upgrade, and the notes say what the review established. THE LEGACY ENTRIES ARE GONE WITH THE SCHEME. Nine of them were here - the whole v0.0.1-beta line the products published before the naming change - and so were three exclusions recording versions that were passed over when the registry was built. None of those strings is a version any more: the shape rule refuses the v-prefixed form, so the catalog could neither identify them nor offer them, and keeping them would have been a list nothing could match. The exclusions are the part worth remarking on: they recorded real decisions (beta1 and beta2 predate the registry; beta5 was skipped by the commit that added beta6 and beta7). Those decisions are kept in the ledger rather than here, because a document that names versions cannot carry decisions about names that are no longer versions.
